clue.text: Alarm gripping front of stalls, not one high up in the gods

definitions.text: not one high up in the gods

indicators.note: to grip something is to hold it tight inside, so one word closes round another

parts.note: sudden alarm or fear

indicators.note: 'front of' keeps only the first letter of 'stalls'

parts.note: the first letter of stalls

explanation.surface: A theatregoer panics in the stalls, far below the cheap seats up in the gods.
explanation.walkthrough: The theatre words (stalls, the gods) set the scene, but the gods here are real deities. A panisc is a little Pan, a minor woodland god.
explanation.definitionFit: A panisc is an inferior rustic deity, a lesser follower of Pan, so it is not one of the lofty Olympians.

clue.text: Participant in coup hurled rock

parts.note: to put a shot is to hurl it
schist is a layered metamorphic rock

explanation.surface: A rebel in an uprising throws a stone.
explanation.definitionFit: A putsch is a sudden attempt to overthrow a government, and a putschist is one who takes part.

clue.text: Indifference, alas, about course

indicators.note: 'about' here means around, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: ay is an old exclamation of sorrow, like alas
a course or route

explanation.surface: A sigh of regret at someone's lack of concern for the course they are on.
explanation.definitionFit: Apathy is a lack of interest or concern, the state of not caring.

clue.text: It circles northern peak, curving inwards

indicators.note: to circle something is to go right round it

parts.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for northern
ben is a Scottish mountain peak, as in Ben Nevis

explanation.surface: Something winds round a mountain in the north on a bending route.
explanation.definitionFit: Inbent is an adjective meaning bent or turned inward, so curving towards the inside.

clue.text: Fungus: clipped rings grow together, coming up

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means the letters read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: broken bones knit, growing back together

indicators.note: clipping cuts off the end of a word

parts.note: rings means telephones, and the horn is slang for the telephone

explanation.surface: Mushrooms whose rings grow together as they push up out of the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry the reversed piece reads upward and so sits on top. 'Rings' looks like fairy rings of fungus but is a verb meaning telephones.
explanation.definitionFit: The stinkhorn is a foul-smelling fungus with a tall phallic stalk.

clue.text: One doing time in prison, not made to pay penalty?

parts.note: surface reading: an inmate serving a sentence
setter's reading: a playful question tagged on, perhaps hinting that the convict trimmed short has escaped the full penalty

explanation.surface: A prisoner serving time who seemingly escaped any fine.
explanation.walkthrough: The short word for a convict fits; the questioning second half is a teasing extra rather than a separate definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Con is short for convict, a person serving a prison sentence.

clue.text: Mixture of RE and ale in religious school? I can certainly stir the crowds up

definitions.text: I can certainly stir the crowds up

indicators.note: 'in' places the mixed letters inside the school

parts.note: a cheder is a Jewish elementary school teaching Hebrew and religion

indicators.note: a mixture blends things together, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written; RE is religious education

explanation.surface: A school mixing scripture lessons with beer boasts that it can rouse a crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition speaks in the first person, as the answer itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheerleader's job is to whip up a crowd's enthusiasm at a sporting event.

clue.text: Was in session longer than quotas arranged, queen having left on time

indicators.note: arranging puts the letters into a fresh order
something that has left is no longer there, so that letter drops out

parts.note: taken as written
Q is the usual abbreviation for queen
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A committee overran its allotted time while sorting out quotas after the queen departed.
explanation.walkthrough: Take Q out of the letters of quotas, add T, and rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To outsit is to sit, or stay in session, longer than another; outsat is its past tense.

clue.text: Voiture with bit of rust obscured? It's crazy to overbid

indicators.note: crazy means mixed up, so the remaining letters are rearranged
something obscured is hidden from view, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: French for car, taken as written
the first letter of rust

explanation.surface: At auction, offering too much for an old French car with hidden rust would be mad.
explanation.definitionFit: To outvie is to outdo in competition, as when bidding beyond a rival at an auction.

clue.text: Dilute what's put into nog for Jack in US

indicators.note: asks which letters must be inserted into one word to make another, so those are what remain

parts.note: taken as written; nog is a kind of strong ale or eggnog
in American slang, jack means nothing at all, as in 'you don't know jack'

explanation.surface: A recipe query about watering down eggnog for an American called Jack.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer is whatever must go inside nog to spell the word Americans mean by jack.
explanation.definitionFit: To thin a liquid is to dilute it, making it weaker or less concentrated.

clue.text: The lady netting small island coley

indicators.note: netting something catches and holds it inside

parts.note: the female pronoun
an ait is a small island in a river

explanation.surface: A woman fishing off a little island lands a coley.
explanation.definitionFit: Saithe is another name for the coley or coalfish, a North Atlantic food fish related to cod.

clue.text: The old endure 'adult-extra'!

parts.note: A is the film-certificate abbreviation for adult
in cricket a bye is an extra, a run scored without the bat touching the ball

explanation.surface: Old folk put up with a film's 'adult-extra' scenes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The old' marks an archaic verb, not elderly people.
explanation.definitionFit: Abye is an archaic verb meaning to pay the penalty for, and so to suffer or endure.

clue.text: Prince enthusiastic about a horse

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for prince
being into something means being keen on it

explanation.surface: A royal who is mad about horses, as many are.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinto is a piebald or skewbald horse, patched with white.

clue.text: Old cradle-song that's hard on ayah busy rocking? Not always

indicators.note: rocking shakes things about, so the letters are jumbled
'not' tells the solver to leave the following word's letters out of the mix

parts.note: H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard
taken as written; an ayah is a nursemaid in India
ay (or aye) is an old word for always

explanation.surface: A nanny rocking a cradle finds the old lullaby hard going, though not every time.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove AY from the letters of ayah busy, shuffle the rest and put H in front. The question mark and 'Not always' look like a comment on the nanny.
explanation.definitionFit: Hushaby is a lullaby word used to soothe a baby to sleep, now rather dated.

clue.text: Curtain girl put round end of cradle — made of this?

definitions.note: refers back to the curtain: the fabric such a curtain might be made of

parts.note: a tab is a theatre curtain

indicators.note: putting one thing round another encloses it

parts.note: bint is slang for a girl

indicators.note: 'end of' keeps only the last letter of 'cradle'

parts.note: the last letter of cradle

explanation.surface: A nursery curtain made by a girl and draped round the end of a cradle.
explanation.walkthrough: Bint is dated British slang for a girl. The definition is the closing question, pointing back at the curtain.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabbinet is a watered fabric of silk and wool, used for upholstery and hangings such as curtains.

clue.text: Lever turns weapon with shaft

parts.note: a hand is a turn at play, as in a round of cards
a pike is a long-shafted spear

explanation.surface: A mechanism that rotates a shafted weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A handspike is a wooden bar used as a lever, for example on a ship's capstan.

clue.text: Tender cep, minced serving as entrée?

indicators.note: mincing chops something up, so the letters are cut and reassembled

parts.note: taken as written; a cep is a mushroom

explanation.surface: Chopped tender mushroom offered as a starter.
explanation.walkthrough: Entrée is used in its sense of a way in or introduction, not a dish.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective precedent means going before; an entrée is an introductory course that comes first.

clue.text: Troughs, back to front? Wherein pigs are found rarely

indicators.note: the last letter is brought round from the back to the front of the word

parts.note: a tye is a trough for washing ore

explanation.surface: A puzzled look at troughs and where pigs are seldom found.
explanation.walkthrough: Move the final S of TYES to the front. 'Rarely' marks a rare spelling: stye is an uncommon form of sty.
explanation.definitionFit: A sty is a pigpen, and stye is a rare variant spelling of that word.

clue.text: He goes without paying stotinki (200 at least), rent misplaced

parts.note: a hundred stotinki make a Bulgarian lev, so 200 is at least two leva

indicators.note: misplaced letters are put in the wrong order, so they need rearranging

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tenant skips off without paying, his rent in Bulgarian coins gone astray.
explanation.walkthrough: The stotinka is a hundredth of the Bulgarian lev, whose plural is leva.
explanation.definitionFit: To levant is to abscond with debts unpaid, especially gambling debts, so a levanter is a defaulter who runs off.

clue.text: SA flower in cleft before enveloping niche, grown wild

parts.note: a narrow crack

indicators.note: to envelop is to wrap around, so one word encloses the next

parts.note: ere is an old word for before

indicators.note: something grown wild is out of order, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A South African flower growing wild in a cleft of rock, filling a niche.
explanation.walkthrough: SA is South Africa. 'Before' is the old word ere, not a positional instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: The chinkerinchee, or chincherinchee, is a white-flowered South African plant of the lily family.

clue.text: Bit of extra canvas, unless it's stormy … i.e. this may appear

indicators.note: a storm throws everything about, so the letters are disordered
says the answer is what shows up beside the named letters, so those are taken away

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sailor sets an extra sail unless the weather turns rough.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of 'unless it' rearrange to the answer plus IE: take out I and E and the rest is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A stuns'l is a studding sail, an additional sail set beyond the main sails in light winds.

clue.text: Fly annoyed by way of piercing

indicators.note: piercing goes into something, so one word sits inside another

parts.note: what's eating you? means what is annoying you
via means by way of

explanation.surface: An irritating insect bites its way through the skin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fly' looks like the insect but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To aviate is to pilot an aircraft, a formal word for flying.

clue.text: Refits damaged sprinkler

indicators.note: damaged things are broken up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A broken garden sprinkler gets repaired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sprinkler' suggests a garden hose; it is the kitchen kind that scatters sugar or flour.
explanation.definitionFit: A sifter is a perforated container used for sprinkling flour or sugar, as a dredger does.

clue.text: Nothing in tin will do for slummock

indicators.note: 'in' places one word inside the other

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
love is nothing, a zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: An empty tin is good enough for a slob.
explanation.definitionFit: Slummock is a dialect word for an untidy, slovenly person, which is just what a sloven is.

clue.text: What's possibly cerebrotonic and may be turned into vers libre?

indicators.note: turning letters about changes their order, so this word can be made from another set

parts.note: taken as written; vers libre is free verse

explanation.surface: A literary musing on whether a brainy, inward temperament could be rendered as free verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' looks like a link to the verse, but its letters are part of the fodder. Cerebrotonic describes the shy, inward-looking temperament in an old body-type theory.
explanation.definitionFit: Introversible means capable of introversion, of being turned inward, which fits the withdrawn cerebrotonic type.

clue.text: Bit of old gold one put into dresses making comeback

indicators.note: a comeback runs the other way, so the whole is read backwards
putting one thing into another places it inside

parts.note: to dress (down) is to thrash, and to larrup is to beat
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An antique gold fragment turns up again sewn into a fashionable dress.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes into LARRUPS after its second letter, and the result is read backwards. 'Bit' here means a coin, as in threepenny bit.
explanation.definitionFit: The spur-rial was a gold coin of James I's reign, so a historical piece of gold money.

clue.text: One aloft, climbing, getting mountain sickness

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means the letters read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: an means one
up high

explanation.surface: A climber high on a peak falls ill with altitude sickness.
explanation.definitionFit: Puna is the name for altitude sickness in the Andes, where the high plateau is also called the puna.

clue.text: Wrap that's sexy if outer parts are removed?

indicators.note: taking away the outer parts leaves only the inner letters

parts.note: erotic means sexy

explanation.surface: A garment that only looks alluring when the outer layers come off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrap' sounds like a shawl but is the food: a roti is wrapped round a filling.
explanation.definitionFit: A roti is an Indian or Caribbean flatbread, often rolled round a curry filling as a wrap.

clue.text: Keep vendetta in the past

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one's keep, the board and sustenance that maintain a person
second meaning: Spenser's old word for a feud

explanation.surface: Cling to an old grudge, keeping a feud alive from long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep' reads as a verb, but it is the noun meaning upkeep. The feud sense is Spenserian, hence 'in the past'.
explanation.definitionFit: Earning one's keep means paying for meals and lodging, and Spenser used the same spelling for enmity or feud.

clue.text: Changing diet, avid for something dietitians may frown on

indicators.note: changing the words alters the order of their letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone keen on a new diet, eager for a treat their nutritionist would disapprove of.
explanation.definitionFit: Artificial food additives such as preservatives and colourings are often discouraged by nutrition professionals.

clue.text: Pistol made of old copper and silver

parts.note: d was the old abbreviation for a penny, a copper coin before decimalisation
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A gun fashioned from copper and silver.
explanation.definitionFit: A dag is a heavy old-fashioned pistol of the sixteenth century.

clue.text: Deny dignity to old Earl after frantic taunts

indicators.note: after places the first piece behind the second one in the answer
frantic means wild and disordered, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
E is the abbreviation for earl

explanation.surface: An earl is stripped of honour after a storm of wild jeers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old' belongs to the definition, marking the word as archaic, not to the earl.
explanation.definitionFit: To unstate, in Shakespeare's day, was to strip someone of rank or dignity.

clue.text: Fruit with one seed in cake? Never!

indicators.note: 'in' says the letters sit inside the words that follow, running across them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A baker scoffs at the idea of putting a single seed into a cake.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark and exclamation hide the run of letters across 'cake' and 'Never'.
explanation.definitionFit: An akene, or achene, is a small dry fruit that holds a single seed and does not split open.

clue.text: GI's kitbag is packed in course of farewell

indicators.note: something packed in the course of another sits inside it

parts.note: vale is Latin for farewell
taken as written

explanation.surface: A soldier packs his kitbag while saying his goodbyes.
explanation.definitionFit: A valise is a soldier's kitbag as well as a small travelling case.

clue.text: Rare ruler, one of ours protected by noble formerly

indicators.note: being protected by something means being surrounded by it

parts.note: gent is an obsolete word for noble or well-born
ER, Elizabeth Regina, was then one of Britain's monarchs

explanation.surface: A seldom-seen monarch, one of our own, guarded by an old nobleman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rare' marks the word as rare in use, not the ruler as uncommon.
explanation.definitionFit: A gerent is a governor or manager, someone who rules or directs; the word is seldom used.
